messages.author: c02c4bf2101897a8
messages.subject: Question to function from_to()
parts:
I have a question about the function from_to(). I use this function to generate the input day by day.
However, I would like it not to generate an input at the beginning of a new day, but sometime the next day and that there might be days where no input is generated.
Is that possible?

Thanks

Krocki

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Question to function from_to()
parts:
Could you provide an example of what you are using and what you want to achieve, please?

Also, note that to(), from(), from_to()... are helpers for common patterns. Some patterns may not fit in any of them, in which case, you'll need to provide your own implementation. The code for those helpers would be a good start [1]. And if you happen to identify a new pattern and build a helper for it, it would be very welcome as a PR to include it in simmer. :)

[1] https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/blob/master/R/generators.R
On Wed, 13 May 2020 at 15:03, Krocki26412 <a.i.a-c...@t-online.de> wrote:

I have a question about the function from_to(). I use this function to generate the input day by day.
However, I would like it not to generate an input at the beginning of a new day, but sometime the next day and that there might be days where no input is generated.
Is that possible?

Thanks

Krocki

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Question to function from_to()
parts:
On Wed, 13 May 2020 at 17:04, Krocki26412 <a.i.a-c...@t-online.de> wrote:
This helps to solve the problem that on the new day a customer is not generated right at the beginning. But on the first day there is no customer at time 0. How can I change this?
Does one customer matter? If so, add another generator with just one customer at t=0.
And how can I solve the problem that no customers are generated on a day?

That's not possible with from_to(). You need to write your own, or place a resource at the beginning of the trajectory that rejects customers on specific days, or generate your timings "offline" and then plug them as a data frame with add_dataframe.

--
Iñaki Úcar
